files.review_notes: All code read and compared with primary EXTRA-0032..0043/RULE-0212, replica EXTRA-0010..0017 and independent BF-0124..0130. Required inventory, duplicate decision shingles, same-line owner references, routing/section checks, privacy and hooks already covered. K0 strips quoted scalar names, so the L1 quote-name issue does not carry over. Two fence predicates, broader empty-directory enforcement and an uncertain inline-path-list representation retained.

claims.claim: A triple-backtick-recognized fenced block left open at the end of an inspected instruction body produces an instruction-check error.
claims.trigger: A non-code instruction artifact has an opening backtick fence with no recognized closing line
claims.exceptions: The helper recognizes lines beginning with at least three backticks; other fence syntaxes are outside this predicate. Section-heading helper calls suppress its reports, while artifact checks report them at 199.
claims.enforcement_effect: Adds an instruction error; standalone CLI exits 1 if any errors exist.

baseline_comparisons.reason: Fence parsing is implementation-classified; malformed fences are mentioned but no separate effective predicate is registered.
Artifact/header requirements and filename classification do not specify fenced-block closure.

claims.comparison_reason: Header-valid correctly classified instructions can still fail solely because a fence remains open; the structural claims omit this condition.
claims.distinguishing_behavioral_scenario: An otherwise valid knowledge skill ends after an opening ```csharp block; fence parser reports code fence is never closed.

claims.claim: Once a backtick fence is open, a backtick-prefixed closing candidate is accepted only when its trimmed line is exactly three backticks.
claims.trigger: A backtick-prefixed line is encountered inside an already open recognized fenced block
claims.exceptions: Leading/trailing whitespace is allowed by trim; this states the checker's exact accepted representation without claiming all Markdown forms are equivalent.
claims.enforcement_effect: Any other recognized candidate line emits the closing-fence error and leaves the block open.

baseline_comparisons.reason: Fence parsing is implementation-classified; malformed fences are mentioned but no separate effective predicate is registered.
Artifact/header requirements and filename classification do not specify fenced-block closure.

claims.comparison_reason: Balanced opening and closing marker counts do not establish acceptance: the closing candidate must have this exact three-backtick representation, a separate check from end-of-file closure.
claims.distinguishing_behavioral_scenario: A body opens with four backticks and later has four backticks on a standalone line; the checker rejects that closing candidate because trim() is not exactly three backticks.

claims.claim: The instruction checker reports an empty directory anywhere reached by its repository-root walk, including outside .claude and docs.
claims.trigger: The whole-repository walk at line 324 reaches a directory with no entries
claims.exceptions: Traversal skips named .hook-state, node_modules, .git, bin, obj and dist directories. This is not every possible filesystem directory.
claims.enforcement_effect: walk('') reuses the empty-directory error at 131 while searching for duplicate decision rows; thus the error has broader scope than the initial .claude/docs inventory walks.

baseline_comparisons.reason: This effective error is registered only inside .claude or docs; root walk applies beyond that scope.
Avoiding speculative/empty trees is general guidance about creating structure, not this unqualified mechanical error on all visited empty directories.
Filename/header failures and duplicate-decision searches do not register the broader empty-directory effect of the reused walk.

claims.comparison_reason: The checker can reject an existing intentional empty runtime-data directory outside the instruction system even without adding speculative architecture.
claims.distinguishing_behavioral_scenario: A project has an empty root/runtime-data directory for generated local output; the root duplicate-decision walk produces an empty-directory error despite instruction artifacts being valid.

claims.claim: An inline YAML paths list in a backend-scoped standard is retained as a scalar and rejected by the scope-territory check, while the equivalent block list is parsed as paths.
claims.actor: Instruction checker frontmatter parser and scope predicate
claims.trigger: Backend standard uses paths: ["backend/**/*.cs"] instead of an indented dash list
claims.exceptions: Common scope accepts any parsed glob. This concerns checker representation, not a claim about host frontmatter support.
claims.enforcement_effect: Parser line 95 stores the bracketed text unchanged; [].concat at 217 wraps it as one string, and globInScope at 111 fails its backend/ prefix.

baseline_comparisons.reason: Non-empty in-scope globs are registered, without the block-versus-inline representation restriction.
Parser implementation and list/procedure/owner-reference restrictions do not represent inline YAML path-list rejection.

claims.comparison_reason: Two list representations can name identical path strings but produce different checker results. Host applicability and whether the unintended restriction is normative remain open.
claims.distinguishing_behavioral_scenario: A backend standard changes only from paths followed by '- backend/**/*.cs' to the bracketed inline representation and gains an out-of-territory error.
claims.open_question: Is this frontend representation accepted by the instruction host, and should this checker-specific restriction count independently?
claims.next_evidence_strategy: Use a pure frontmatter/scope-function probe and compare declared syntax requirements in executable and modality passes.
